intent.text: From the every-session vantage: a global allow rule is felt by every Claude session on the machine, including ones whose agents never agreed to it, and it takes effect live. My recommendation is REMOVE the global rule, or at minimum do not keep it unconditionally. Reasons: (1) The rule's safety rests on the claim that a command after the export is judged on its own. That is measured only for one case (a test touch). Permission matchers that treat a bare trailing `*` as matching anything can admit `export CC_AGENT=x; <anything>` or `&&`-chained commands if the compound-command split is not applied to the rewritten string. The README did not test `;`, `&&`, `|`, newlines, or backticks after the export. (2) Two PreToolUse hooks both rewriting Bash is unverified, so the string the permission check sees may not be what the README assumes. (3) The rule is a blanket grant on a value that is partly controlled by the caller. If the identity key or parent fields contain shell metacharacters or quotes, the matcher could be fooled. Conditions if kept: test these shapes in a throwaway project before keeping it: `export CC_AGENT='x'; rm -f file`, `&&`, `|`, newline-separated, and a value with embedded `'`. Preferably move the rule into a project-scoped settings file for the agent-identity work, not the global file, so other sessions are not affected. Until those tests run, I favor remove.
